skill.name: environment-setup-guide
skill.description: Guide developers through development environment setup, including tools, dependencies, configuration files, and verification steps.
skill.summary: Create clear setup instructions for local development environments across common platforms.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown documentation false positives, such as code fences, example .env files, localhost URLs, and visible setup commands. Confirmed risks remain where the guide encourages unverified remote installer execution, elevated Docker privilege changes, and weak copy-paste database credentials.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands execute downloaded scripts directly.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell and PowerShell iex examples with official manual install steps, checksum verification, or clear review instructions before execution.

remediation.issue: Docker setup grants the user Docker daemon access.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that docker group membership can provide root-equivalent access and require explicit user confirmation before recommending the change.

remediation.issue: Example database configuration uses password as a default credential.
remediation.suggestion: Use generated placeholders and tell users to create unique local credentials instead of copying fixed passwords.

remediation.issue: Environment examples mention secret-bearing files and keys.
remediation.suggestion: Keep only placeholder values in documentation and add guidance to store real secrets outside committed files.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Remote Installer Execution Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The guide recommends installer flows that download scripts from the network and execute them through a shell or PowerShell, including elevated execution. This can normalize copy-paste execution of unverified remote code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple examples combine network download with immediate shell or privileged execution. The context is legitimate setup documentation, but the unsafe pattern is explicit and repeatable.

semantic_findings.title: Weak Default Database Credentials in Example
semantic_findings.description: The Docker example uses a simple postgres password in the connection string and database service configuration. Users may copy these defaults into shared or persistent development environments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The password value is plainly visible in the Docker Compose example. It appears intended for local development, so the risk is moderate rather than malicious.

content.value_statement: Development setup often fails because tools, versions, and configuration steps are unclear. This skill turns project requirements into structured setup instructions with verification and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Identifies required languages, package managers, databases, and developer tools for a project.
Drafts platform-specific setup steps for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
Adds environment variable and configuration file guidance for common project types.
Creates verification steps to confirm tools, services, and dependencies work.
Includes troubleshooting advice for path, permission, port, and database issues.
Provides a setup script template for repeatable local onboarding.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not install tools by itself.
Some install commands need review before use on production or managed devices.
Project-specific versions and secrets must come from the user or repository documentation.
Commands may need adjustment for nonstandard operating systems or restricted networks.

use_cases.title: Onboard a New Developer
use_cases.description: Create a complete local setup checklist for a project with install, configuration, and verification steps.

use_cases.title: Document a Project Environment
use_cases.description: Turn scattered setup notes into a clear guide for tools, dependencies, services, and environment variables.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Setup Failures
use_cases.description: Build troubleshooting steps for command path errors, permission failures, busy ports, and database connection issues.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Setup Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a development environment setup guide for this project. Include required tools, install steps, environment variables, and verification commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add Platform-Specific Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this setup guide for macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows. Keep each platform separate and include clear verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Environment Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Help diagnose these setup errors. Explain likely causes, checks to run, and fixes for each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Automated Setup Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe automated setup plan for this project. Include prerequisites, manual approval points, verification, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: A Node.js project needs onboarding instructions for a new team member.
output: A prerequisite list covering Node.js, npm, Git, and database requirements.
Platform-specific installation guidance with version checks.
Environment file setup steps and a final project startup checklist.

output_examples.input: A Python web app fails during local setup.
output: A troubleshooting checklist for Python version, virtual environment activation, dependencies, and database connectivity.
Suggested verification commands and expected results.
Notes about environment variables that must be supplied by the project owner.

output_examples.input: A team wants repeatable Docker-based setup instructions.
output: A structured Docker setup plan with prerequisites, service startup steps, and health checks.
Warnings for credentials, local ports, and host permissions.
A maintenance checklist for updating versions and testing clean installs.

best_practices: Review install commands before running them, especially commands that use sudo or download remote scripts.
Use placeholders for secrets and document where real values should be obtained securely.
Test setup instructions on a clean machine before sharing them with a team.
anti_patterns: Do not copy remote installer commands into production systems without verification.
Do not store real API keys or passwords in example files or documentation.
Do not assume all developers use the same operating system, shell, or package manager.

faq.question: Does this skill install software automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps create instructions and checks that a developer can review and run manually.

faq.question: Can it support macOS, Linux, and Windows?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed to produce platform-specific setup guidance for common development tools.

faq.question: Can it handle environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes. It can document required variables and example files, but real secrets should be stored securely.

faq.question: Is it useful for Docker projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Docker installation, Compose services, verification, and common local issues.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the project language, required versions, package manager, services, operating systems, and known setup errors.

faq.question: Can it create troubleshooting sections?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize fixes for missing commands, permissions, ports, dependencies, and database connections.
